metadata.title: Supply Chain Stocks Sink Amid Wall Street Sell-Off, Though Air Freight Shows Resilience

content.text:
It's been a tough week for major indices, as a convergence of factors has led investors to flee Wall Street. And the major publicly traded stocks in the sourcing and supply chain industry were not immune to the selloff.
Dragging down stocks were AI value fatigue and doubts about any worthy ROI on AI infrastructure. For example, even though Anthropic staged a blockbuster IPO on Nov. 19 and surged in its stock exchange debut, regulatory filings showed massive operating losses of about $104 billion over the first nine months of 2026. This reinforced market anxiety and triggered a sharp afternoon reversal in major AI hardware and cloud names like Nvidia, Micron and CoreWeave. There were also ongoing concerns about the headwinds facing chipmakers. Interest rate pressure didn't help either.
More from WWD
As a result, over 90 percent of S&P 500 stocks declined on Thursday, Nov. 19.
From Nov. 12 through the close on Nov. 19, the market clocked a six-session losing streak for the S&P 500 and a drop of more than 5 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 6.12 percent during that period while the Nasdaq Composite lost 5.9 percent. And the Russell 2000 declined 5.14 percent.
From Nov. 13 through Nov. 19, stocks across the logistics, ground freight, air freight and supply chain sectors mostly pulled back alongside a broader market sell-off on Nov. 19. The benchmark iShares U.S. Transportation ETF (IYT) fell roughly 3.4 percent over the period. And while broad freight demand and industrial volume concerns pressured rails and trucking, air freight and global forwarding companies showed relative resilience—supported by strong third-quarter earnings, AI-hyperscaler air cargo demand and recent investor day updates.
In the integrated parcel and air freight segment, United Parcel Service dropped about 2.9 percent over the week, slipping from a Nov. 13 close of $112.40 to $109.11 on Nov. 19. Shares pulled back in tandem with broader transportation weakness despite strong post-third quarter momentum.
FedEx Corporation fell about 2.8 percent over the week, moving from $323.73 on Nov. 13 to $314.64 at the Nov. 19 close. The stock dropped for three consecutive sessions ending Nov. 19, although it had outperformed the S&P 500 during Thursday's broader market drop. And DHL Group traded around $32.09, down 2.1 percent on Nov. 19, but holding onto earlier November gains after the company's management highlighted strong air cargo contributions driving a 16 percent profit increase for the third quarter.
